rule: Truss Chords - Joints U6 to U13 incl., U20, U21, U22, L6 to L15 incl., L20, L21 and L22: 1 1/4 in. dia high strength rivets to connect chord webs to gusset plates, splice plates and fillers

rule: Joints U0 to U5 incl., U14 to U19 incl., L0 to L5 incl., and L16 to L19 incl.: 1 1/8 in. dia high strength rivets to connect chord webs to gusset plates, splice plates and fillers
note: U14 / U15 are 1 1/8 in (p.82 note previously read 1 1/4 for U14: see README Corrections)

rule: All Cover Plate Splices: 1 1/8 in. dia high strength rivets
Truss Verticals and Diagonals: 1 1/8 in. dia high strength rivets for these members to gussets, except 1 1/4 in. for both ends of U11-L11 and the U11 end of L10-U11 and U11-L12
All Truss Members: 1 in. dia carbon steel stitch rivets, unless noted
Floor System: 7/8 in. dia carbon steel rivets, unless noted
Bracing: all rivets in bracing gusset plates 1 in. dia carbon steel unless noted; stitch rivets 7/8 in. dia carbon steel
All 1 1/8 in. and 1 1/4 in. rivets regardless of location, and whether shop or field, must be high strength rivets
note: all solid dots and field rings of the 1 1/8 / 1 1/4 in groups are HS rivets

rule: For sealing, pitch on a single line adjacent to a free edge of an outside plate or shape not to exceed 4 + 4t, nor 7 in.; with a second staggered line at gage less than 1 1/2 + 4t the stagger pitch not to exceed 4 in. + 4t - 3/4 g, nor 7 in. - 3/4 g, but need not be less than half the single-line requirement; t = thickness (in.) of thinner outside plate or shape

In compression members the pitch in any single line in the direction of stress not to exceed 12t; staggered adjacent lines with gage less than the maximum 24t: stagger pitch not to exceed 12t nor 15t - 3/8 g
High strength rivets (shop and field): shear 20,000 psi, bearing 40,000 psi on silicon steel / 27,000 psi on carbon steel; carbon steel rivets: shear 13,500 psi, bearing 27,000 psi

Holes for truss joints, including gusset plates, splice plates and fillers, punched or drilled 15/16 in. and reamed to size; holes for stitch rivets punched or drilled 15/16 in. and reamed assembled to 1 1/16 in.
Holes punched or drilled 11/16 in. and reamed assembled to 15/16 in. unless noted
Holes for splices punched or drilled 11/16 in. and reamed to 15/16 in. with parts assembled, or to a metal templet; other holes may be punched full size
Bracing and diaphragms: holes may be punched full size unless noted; expansion dams and supports: drilled, sub-punched, reamed as noted on the design details

Chords: 2 - 1 1/8 in. dia holes in the bottom flange region and manholes 12 in. (11 1/2 in. at L10-L11 and L11-L12); 5 - 1 1/4 in. or 1 3/8 in. dia holes (see notes) in the chord web; diagonals 21 / 24 / 26 in. webs and 18 in. channel webs: 2 - 1 1/8 in. dia holes, 4 - 1 1/4 in. holes (webs), 12 in. manholes; verticals 18 in. channel webs: 2 - 1 1/8 in. holes; 12 in. manholes
note: cross-section sketches at the bottom of the stress sheet; gage digits (3 1/2, 4 1/2, 5 1/2 ...) not transcribed

rule: Suspenders (4 in. dia bridge rope, breaking strength 730 T): panel points 14 / 15,17,19,21 / 16,20 / 18 / 22 design loads +348 / +412 / +378 / +322 / +348 kips; point 14 is a rope with steel section (N.A. 169.19, gross 249.50)
note: table at the top of the sheet; used by the suspender models

rule: Trusses cambered for total dead load deflection; cambered lengths calculated from areas determined per AASHO Art. 3.6.10, increased 10 % for the effect of details; stringer and floor beam camber see sheet 32

Wide flange sections forming horizontal or nearly horizontal troughs: drain holes as typical details; anchor bolt holes in masonry plates and shoes filled with molten zinc after erection; manhole spacing in the details is approximate and manholes in web members of trusses and bracing shall be alternated on opposite sides
